concerns.text: Task T010 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it updates `model_results.json` produced by T008, creating a hidden ordering requirement. `[P]` tasks must not share mutable artifacts; this violates the parallel‑safety rule.

Task T011 is tagged `[P]` yet it reads `model_results.json` (produced by T008/T010) and `cv_mse_per_fold` added by T010. It therefore depends on prior tasks and cannot be safely run in parallel with them.

Task T012 (report assembly) is marked `[P]` but it links to artifacts (`features.csv`, `model_results.json`, `residuals_plot.png`) generated by earlier tasks, establishing an implicit ordering dependency.

Task T013 (end‑to‑end pipeline driver) is `[P]` yet it sequentially invokes scripts that produce and consume the same files (e.g., `model_results.json`), so it cannot be run concurrently with those producers/consumers.

Task T014 (quick‑start guide) is `[P]` but references the command `python code/main.py`, which depends on the successful completion of earlier tasks. This creates an ordering requirement contrary to the parallel‑safe tag.

Task T015 (full test suite execution) is `[P]` yet it must run after the pipeline (T013) and after all test files are added (e.g., T007, T011). It therefore has a hidden dependency and is not parallel‑safe.
Task T016 (resource‑monitoring wrapper) is `[P]` but is imported by every script, meaning it must exist before any of those scripts execute. This creates an implicit ordering constraint.
